title: Python: First Programs
summary: Write real Python from the first lesson: input and output, decisions, loops, lists and functions. Every lesson runs in the Code studio in your browser, with a marked leap-year lab and practice challenges.
outcomes: Write Python programs that read input, calculate and print results
Make decisions with if, elif, else, and combine conditions with and, or and not
Repeat work with for and while loops over lists and ranges
Write and test functions that return values
prerequisites: None. You need a browser; nothing to install.

questions.explanation: Always text. Convert with int() or float() before doing maths.

questions.prompt: Which line prints "Ada is 16" when name = "Ada" and age = 16?
questions.explanation: The f before the quote makes it an f-string. The third option fails: you cannot add text and a number.

lessons.title: if, elif, else, and, or, not
Lab: leap years
lessons.intro: Write is_leap(year), run the examples, then check it on fresh years. It runs only in your browser.

questions.explanation: The first true condition wins: 70 >= 60, so B. Put the highest band first.

questions.prompt: Which tests for an even number?
questions.explanation: An even number leaves remainder 0 when divided by 2.

options: No: it divides by 100 but not by 400
questions.explanation: Century years must also divide by 400. 2000 is a leap year; 1900 is not.
range stops before its second number.
Counting starts at 0, so [1] is the second item.

questions.prompt: A while loop never stops. What is the likeliest cause?
options: Nothing inside the loop changes the condition
questions.explanation: Something in the loop must eventually make the condition false.

questions.prompt: What does a function return if it has no return line?
questions.explanation: Python functions give back None by default.

questions.prompt: Why do tests check what a function returns rather than what it prints?
options: A returned value can be stored and compared; printed text only goes to the screen
print is not allowed in functions
questions.explanation: Returned values can be used by other code, including tests.

questions.prompt: def area(w, h): return w * h. What is area(3, 4)?
Which is a valid variable name in Python?
questions.explanation: Letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit, no spaces or dashes.
